name: Casein hydrolyzate
description: Casein hydrolyzate (CAS 65072-00-6 ), also marketed under the trade name N-Z Amine, is produced by enzymatic or acid hydrolysis of casein protein. This process yields a mixture of peptides and free amino acids. It functions as a bioavailable nitrogen source and flavor contributor across food, pharmaceutical, and agricultural applications. In food manufacturing, it delivers savory, umami-forward flavor profiles to soups and sauces. It is frequently used in seasonings and processed meat products where clean-label protein hydrolysates are specified. Pharmaceutical and nutraceutical formulators use it as a nitrogen source in culture media. It also serves as a peptide ingredient in clinical nutrition products targeting protein supplementation. In animal feed and agricultural fermentation, it supports microbial growth as a readily metabolized nitrogen substrate. It is used in fermentation broths and starter culture media. Infant formula and sports nutrition manufacturers source it as a partially hydrolyzed protein fraction to improve digestibility and reduce allergenicity. Casein hydrolyzate is supplied as a cream to tan-colored powder, with particle size and solubility profiles varying by manufacturer. Standard grades include food-grade and pharmaceutical-grade specifications. Select suppliers offer USP or FCC -compliant material. Degree of hydrolysis and nitrogen content are key specification parameters buyers should confirm when evaluating lots for fermentation use. These parameters are also critical for clinical nutrition applications.
